newsitem.title: UK: Shell says six staff injured, 127 held in Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: Shell says six staff injured, 127 held in Nigeria.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell said on Monday six of its staff were injured during an attack on five oil pumping stations in Nigeria on Saturday.
"Community groups invaded the flow stations in the northern swamp area of the western division," said a Shell spokesman, adding 127 were detained.
Shell said most of the detainees were being held at the Egwa Two supply and logistics base. The company did not know whether any foreign nationals were being held.
Shell said the occupation of the oil installations stemmed from a dispute concerning local government elections held on March 15.
One of the groups had asked Shell to pass on a list of demands to local authorities.
"We have passed the demands on to the state government and are emphasising our approach of non-violence and dialogue," said the Shell spokesman.
"We are trying to establish dialogue with the community groups to resolve the matter," he added.
